motion_prompt.motion_prompt: Create a realistic educational science video clip for Class 12 Chemistry experiment 'Determine the boiling point of an organic compound'. Show the scene 'Manual setup and procedure': A 50 mL beaker on wire gauze and a tripod contains the bath. A clamped thermometer has the ignition tube tied alongside it, with the tube lower end near the thermometer bulb. The bulb and half of the ignition tube are immersed without touching the beaker. A capillary tube has its open end dipped in the organic liquid in the ignition tube. Perform this step: Half-fill a 50 mL glass beaker with water. Seal one end of a capillary tube by heating it in a flame. Put a few drops of the organic liquid in an ignition tube and dip the open capillary end into it. Tie the ignition tube to the thermometer with its lower end near the thermometer bulb. Set the beaker on wire gauze on a tripod and position the thermometer bulb and half of the ignition tube in the water. Show the expected observation: The thermometer bulb and half of the ignition tube are immersed in the bath; the bulb and ignition tube do not touch the beaker. Visible actions may include: Heat the beaker gently, Observe a regular stream of bubbles in the ignition tube, Note the thermometer temperature at the bubbling endpoint. Use only these materials: 50 mL glass beaker, Capillary tube sealed at one end, Ignition tube, Thermometer, Iron stand with clamp, Wire gauze, Tripod stand, Burner or spirit lamp, Thread, Water for the bath, A few drops of an organic liquid sample. Follow these reviewed safety notes: Fix the thermometer so its bulb and the ignition tube do not touch the beaker.; Use liquid paraffin in the beaker instead of water when the boiling point is above 95 degrees Celsius.. Keep the apparatus, quantities, actions, and scientific outcome accurate. Use clear classroom lighting, stable framing, natural motion, and no labels or watermark.
